$comment: Generated copies of server/shared code, written by scripts/gen-shared-mirror.mjs (npm run gen:shared) and checked by npm run lint:shared-mirror. Each entry copies the non-test files of `source` into `target`. transform "none" (the default) is a byte-for-byte copy without a header; "cjs-to-esm" and importRewrite change the text, and then every written file starts with a GENERATED header. include / exclude narrow the file list (paths relative to source); keep lists hand-written files in target that are neither generated nor reported as extra. generatedRoots lists directories that hold only generated targets: --check fails on any non-test file under one that no entry targets.

entries.why: App Studio and the web automation builder: the agent-hub image builds with context ./agent-hub and cannot see server/.
The phone's flow editor evaluates the same conditions; exprVendor.lockstep.test.ts holds it to both originals. index.d.mts is the hand-written type declaration.

App Studio definition model (ids, section style, the shared definition ops, design presets, variables): the editor's state/definitionOps.js and runtime re-export it. The lockstep fixture and golden are test data and stay on the server.
The next-run time of an agent schedule: the wizard and the schedule modal show it, the server's wizard/commit stores it, so both compute it with the same code.

The phone's flow editor maps and deepens with the web's TypeScript mapping library (field tree, deep fields, forEach deepening, auto-map). The JavaScript modules it leans on (loops, listShape, partitionInputs, boundPaths, valueParts, dataSummary, refTokens) and humanizeFieldKey/humanizeFieldTail resolve to the phone's own ports; mobile bindings/*.ts re-export the mirror.
Which output keys are diagnostics; the mirrored deepFields / autoMapListInput import it as ../flow/stepPayload.
Output-field drafts of a step's settings; mobile formState/outputDrafts.ts re-exports it.

Webpage preview document (bridges, inliners, react-mui import map, bundler plugin, runtime guard, asset resolver, shell): the web editor's preview (utils/composeWebpageDocument.js, utils/buildWebpagePreview.js) and the server's screenshot, public React share and phone draft document build the same document.
The webpage-to-markdown component runs from its own directory and cannot require server/; its index.js adds the guarded fetch and the CLI around this converter.
The SSRF guard of the component's fetches (safeGet.js); a component cannot require server/.
The SSRF guard of the component's fetches (safeGet.js); a component cannot require server/.

CMS theme presets: the server is the schema of record (the AI builder applies a theme by name); the panel's themePresets.js re-exports this copy and adds applyPreset. themePresets.lockstep.test.ts deep-equals it to the source.

CMS block defaults and layout variants (BLOCK_DEFAULTS, BLOCK_VARIANTS, design enums): a block added in the panel matches one created server-side. catalogue.js keeps only the editor registry and re-exports these; blockData.lockstep.test.ts deep-equals them to the source.

Themable emoji catalogue: utils/emojiCatalog.js re-exports it (plus defaultEmojiFor / labelFor) as the synchronous fallback before /api/icons/catalog loads. emojiCatalog.lockstep.test.ts deep-equals it to the source.
Matching a table's columns to a step's fields by normalised name: the web's modules and the phone's tablesRowMap share one implementation; formState/columnMatch.ts re-exports it.
Dotted key paths (IDENT_RE, joinKeyPath, keyPickable) over the shared expression path grammar; bindings/keyPath.ts re-exports it.
The Wait step's limits and unit formatting (1 s to 24 h); model/waitDuration.ts re-exports it.
The web form-state record types (FormRecord, JsonValue); the mirrored approvalStages imports it as ./types.
The approval chain's caps and seat/stage sanitising (the server's rulebook): the web's settings and the phone's approval editor share one implementation; formState/approvalStages.ts re-exports it.

Which text is a reference path and how it is spelled, binding <-> input text, the formula/condition text, autocomplete tokens, path walking and previews: the web builder and the phone's flow editor read paths and bindings with the same functions. model/pathGrammar.ts, model/route/bindingText.ts, bindings/{walkPath,conditionText,bindingHelpers}.ts re-export it.

The period the answers dashboard looks at (presets, default, the from/to the fetch sends): the web and the phone share one implementation; web.lockstep.test.ts still runs the fixtures; model/answersRange.ts re-exports it.

The model behind the Now running strip (rollups, tone, order, hidden count, null-not-empty rule): one implementation for web and phone; nowRunning.lockstep.test.ts still runs the fixtures; model/nowRunning.ts adapts the phone's RunFacets (null) to it.
